title: In Vivo Two-Color 2-Photon Imaging of Genetically-Tagged Reporter Cells in the Skin
protocol: Prepare a 5 μg/20 μL solution of lipopolysaccharide-FITC in sterile 1x PBS (pH 7.4).
Vortex the stock solution at medium intensity for at least 30 seconds to ensure homogenous mixing.
Do not place LPS into a glass container; use siliconized microcentrifuge tubes if possible.
Keep the solution on ice until use.
Set up the multiphoton system for two-color imaging.
Use two separate excitation lasers, a GFP/RFP filter cube set, and a 25x (1.05 NA) water-immersion objective.
Place a stereotaxic apparatus on the stage of the multiphoton microscope.
Connect the stereotaxic apparatus to an anesthesia delivery machine.
Place a piece of matte black paper on the surface of the apparatus as a connection point for the mouse paw.
Select the resonant scanner with a fixed scan area of 512 μm x 512 μm.
Place the mouse into the induction chamber of the anesthesia delivery system.
Use 5% isoflurane at a 2 L/min flow rate of oxygen to place the mouse under deep anesthesia.
Transfer the mouse to the stereotaxic apparatus with access to a nose cone.
Reduce the isoflurane to 1.5%-2%.
Affix the hind paw to a piece of black paper using black tape proximal and distal to the area of interest.
Ensure the plantar surface of the paw is unobstructed and facing up towards the objective.
Place sterile water-based lubricant on the plantar surface of the paw.
Touch the objective to the lubricant to create a column of liquid between the paw and the objective.
Use FITC excitation light to focus into the dermal layer of the paw.
Ensure tdTomato-tagged fibroblasts are visualized before continuing.
Image the area of cells located just below the plantar surface of the hind paw with both the 930 nm and 1100 nm-tuned lasers.
Acquire a 15-minute time-lapse of about 5-10 z-slices at approximately 1 µm per slice.
Perform an intraplantar injection of 5 µg/20 µL LPS-FITC on the mouse’s hind paw using a 25 µL glass Hamilton syringe and 30G needle.
Image an area of cells located just below the plantar surface of the hind paw with both the 930 nm and 1100 nm-tuned lasers after injection.
Acquire a 60-120 minute time-lapse of about 5-10 z-slices at approximately 1 µm per slice to identify uptake of LPS-FITC by cells.
